hook: 50,191 reviews, $29.94 price — here's what convinced me

scenes.visual_prompt: Screen-recording style zoom into a review count badge reading '50,191 ratings'
scenes.voiceover: A few hundred reviews, you can buy. Fifty thousand, you really can't.

scenes.visual_prompt: Scrolling text montage of review snippets: 'weak', 'trickle', 'barely rinses shampoo'
scenes.voiceover: Thousands of reviews on factory showerheads say the same three words.

scenes.visual_prompt: Star rating graphic holding steady at 4.5 across a sliding scale of review count from 100 to 50,000
scenes.voiceover: At that volume, the rating is closer to a population survey than a cherry-picked testimonial.

scenes.visual_prompt: Handheld showerhead product shot with price tag $29.94, spray modes highlighted
scenes.voiceover: The product behind that number: a $29.94 handheld with eight spray modes and scale-resistant nozzles.

scenes.visual_prompt: Honest caveat text card reading 'It can't create pressure your pipes don't have'
scenes.voiceover: It can't manufacture pressure your home's supply line doesn't already deliver — it just stops wasting what's there.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final shot of water running strong, link graphic, price tag
scenes.voiceover: Thirty dollars to test that claim yourself is a low-risk bet.

caption: I don't trust 'amazing' in a product description. I trust 50,191 people rating the same $29.94 showerhead 4.5 stars. Here's what's actually on the spec sheet — link in bio.
